findings.title: Unescaped `embed_url` is written into the stored post as HTML after sanitization, so a crafted URL stores a live event-handler attribute
findings.description: `TopicEmbed.import` builds the footer as `"#{url}"` and appends it to `contents` at line 13. This happens after `import_remote` has run Readability's tag and attribute whitelist, so the footer is never sanitized and `url` is never escaped. The post is then created with `cook_method: raw_html` (line 22), so `Post#cook` returns the string unchanged (`app/models/post.rb:133`), and the embed page prints it with `raw` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19`). An anonymous client can reach this sink: - `EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` with any `embed_url` that has no topic yet (`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`). - The only gate is the Referer host check in `ensure_embeddable` (line 26). Referer is a request header, so any HTTP client can set it to the embeddable host. - `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-19`) checks only the host. Path and query may contain `'`, `=`, `(`, `)`, which the URI parser accepts. For example, `http:///?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` passes the host check. `fetch_http` then calls `open(url)`, which succeeds when the host answers 200 for that URL, as many blogs do for a homepage with a query string. The footer becomes `…`. `absolutize_urls` parses it with Nokogiri and keeps the `onmouseover` attribute. The result is a topic published under the embed user's account. Any reader who hovers the link runs script in the Discourse origin. The same sink takes the feed `link` value from `PollFeed`. Fix by HTML-escaping `url` in the footer, or by building the anchor with Nokogiri. Also reject URLs containing quotes, `<`, `>`, or whitespace before fetching.

findings.title: RSS item HTML is stored and rendered without any sanitizer
findings.description:
`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` decodes entities, so escaped markup in a feed becomes live markup. `TopicEmbed.import` passes it to `PostCreator` as `raw_html`, and it is stored as `cooked` unchanged (`app/models/post.rb:133`). It is rendered with `raw` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19`). Nothing on this path removes `<script>`, `on*` attributes, or `javascript:` URLs. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href` and `src`. Contrast this with `import_remote`, which whitelists tags through Readability.

Severity depends on how much the feed is trusted. Any feed author, or anyone who can change an `http://` feed in transit, gets script execution for every reader. Run the feed HTML through a whitelist sanitizer before storing it.

findings.title: A post rejected by the spam check is treated as saved, so the import crashes and the whole feed poll aborts
findings.description:
`PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` (`lib/post_creator.rb:222-229`) has raised Rollback before the save. The returned post has `id == nil` and has errors. `TopicEmbed.import` only checks `post.present?` (line 24), so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with `post_id: nil`. The column is `null: false` (`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5`), so this raises. The exception rolls back the transaction and escapes the `rss.items.each` loop in `poll_feed.rb:31-37`, which has no rescue. Every item after it is skipped on every hourly run.

The trigger is in `Post#has_host_spam?` (`app/models/post.rb:164-172`). Each post counts as one for its host, plus one for each earlier post by the same user that linked that host. Admins and moderators are exempt (`app/models/user.rb:393-396`). For a non-staff embed user below basic trust, the threshold is 3 (`config/site_settings.yml:325`), so the third post linking the same blog host is rejected. Check `post.persisted?` before creating the embed, and skip rejected items.

findings.title: postMessage origin check is a substring match, so a look-alike origin can resize the iframe
findings.description: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin string that appears inside `discourseUrl`. With `discourseUrl = "https://discuss.example.com/"`, a message from `https://discuss.example.co` passes, because that string is a prefix of the URL. Its `discourse-resize` message can then set `iframe.height` to any value. The impact is limited to resizing the frame, but the check was meant to be an origin allowlist. Compare parsed origins for equality instead, for example by reading `protocol` and `host` from an anchor element built from `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: The Disqus importer aborts the whole run on the first thread it can't fetch
findings.description: The importer used to create one topic per thread without any network access. Now `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` runs `open(url)` for every thread, with no rescue. A 404, a timeout, or a nil `t[:link]` raises out of `parser.threads.each`. Threads imported earlier remain, and the rest are never imported. Rescue per thread, log the failing URL, and continue.

findings.title: The `--category` option was removed from the Disqus importer with no replacement
findings.description: The `method_option :category` declaration and the lookup that used it were removed. Nothing takes its place. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` has no category parameter, and the `category:` argument to `PostCreator` is gone. A script that passes `-c` or `--category` silently loses that behavior. Restore the option and pass the category through `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote`, or document the removal as intentional.

findings.title: `Gemfile.lock` has no entries for the two gems added to the Gemfile
findings.description: `Gemfile:210-211` adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss`. `Gemfile_rails4.lock` lists both (lines 313 and 344). `Gemfile.lock`, the lock for the Rails 3.2.12 app (line 308), lists neither, and `.gitignore` doesn't exclude it. A frozen or deployment install will fail because the Gemfile has dependencies the lock doesn't record. The `*.lock` files were excluded from the diff I was given, so I can't tell whether this commit touched `Gemfile.lock`. The file on disk does not contain the gems. Run `bundle install` and commit the updated lock.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` drops an existing table and its rows
findings.description: `force: true` makes Rails drop `topic_embeds` if it already exists before it creates the table. If the migration runs against a database that has the table but no `schema_migrations` row, every embed mapping is lost. Each embedded article then gets imported again as a new, duplicate topic. The same flag was added to the base-commit migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3`, which is an edit to an existing migration. Remove `force: true` in both places, and restore the top-topics migration to its base-commit form.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` in the embed template is malformed
findings.description: Line 6 closes the `if` from line 2 with `end if`, which is a modifier, not a block terminator. Depending on how Rails 3.2's Erubis handler trims the newline after the tag, this either fails to compile, which would make every embed page with a topic return a 500, or it compiles only by accident. I could not render the template, so I can't say which. Change it to `<%- end %>`.
